text:
Pagerbot: ALERT: gpu-pool eu-west-1-gpu-high queue depth > 95th pct threshold for 6m. paging oncall Anna (severity: P1)

Anna (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming scope — seeing sustained queue growth and token throttles in eu-west. Adding @Sam R and @Infra SRE.

Sam R: I rolled continuous-batching config at 09:12 UTC for rollout/continuous-batching-v2 (small change to reduce max_batch_window to lower latency). Diff: `max_batch_window_ms: 10 -> 2`, `prefix_cache_ttl_s: 300 -> 0` (accidental).

Marta: whoa prefix_cache_ttl -> 0? that effectively turned off prefix cache warm caches. miss rate spiked.

Ravi: metrics: queue depth for eu-west-1-gpu-high climbed from 200 -> 2000 in 10m. per-pool throughput dropped 40%. prefix cache hit-rate dropped 98% -> 2% at 09:14. KV eviction rate up.

Infra SRE: Autoscaler attempted to scale but hit pool_max_nodes cap (config: pool_max_nodes=48). Errors in autoscaler logs: `scale_request rejected: pool_max_nodes reached`.

Sam R: I see repeated `batcher: cannot schedule, cache_miss=true` lines in runtime logs, causing longer SLO paths. Pushing more nodes won't help if cache is cold and batching shrank.

Anna (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan (short list):
- 1) revert continuous-batching-v2 rollout to previous config (target: 09:22 UTC)
- 2) temporarily increase pool_max_nodes to 60 to allow autoscaler headroom
- 3) run prefix-cache warmup job for top-20 models in pool
- 4) rate-limit non-SLA customers (soft throttle) to reduce queue pressure
- 5) if autoscaler still blocked, manual node add via infra override

Marta: I'm executing revert now. starting rollback to continuous-batching-v1 -> applying config `prefix_cache_ttl_s=300` and `max_batch_window_ms=10`.

Deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollback continuous-batching-v2 -> v1 by Marta at 09:22:41 UTC, change-id=c4f3b3

Ravi: pushing pool_max_nodes=60 now (infra override). Command run: `infractl pool update eu-west-1-gpu-high --max-nodes 60 --reason "incident: temp increase"`.

Infra SRE: manual scale requested: adding 6 nodes to eu-west-1-gpu-high (expected capacity +6). monitoring node join.

Sam R: kicked off prefix warmup for top models with warmup script. snippet:
```for model in $(cat top20_models.txt); do
  python tools/prefix_warmup.py --model $model --pool eu-west-1-gpu-high --concurrency 2
done```

Anna (oncall): enacted soft throttles for free-tier customers at 09:28 UTC: `rate_limit: 20 req/min` for affected routes. Not touching enterprise SLAs.

Marta: rollback complete @ 09:24:05. Confirming config now `prefix_cache_ttl_s=300` and `max_batch_window_ms=10`. Runtime reporting immediate improvement in batch sizes.

Ravi: node join complete @ 09:35. autoscaler now has headroom, no more `pool_max_nodes` rejects.

Infra SRE: prefix cache hit-rate trending back up: 2% -> 48% within 8m after warmup started. Throughput slowly recovering.

Sam R: observing decreased tail latency. However some requests still saw 429s earlier. We need to compile customer impact.

Anna (oncall): customer impact quick count: 12 customers with noticeable errors or elevated latency between 09:12–09:30 UTC. Of those, 3 are enterprise with support-critical SLAs (IDs redacted). Support and account teams notified. Estimated affected tenants experienced 5–30s higher latencies or transient 429s.

Marta: posted incident banner on status page at 09:40 UTC: "Degraded performance in eu-west-1, mitigation in progress".

Pagerbot: INCIDENT: incident_eu_west_gpu_high #1767890123 status=mitigating responders=[Anna (oncall), Sam R, Marta, Ravi] pager_count=1

Sam R: root cause summary draft: rollback of continuous-batching config disabled prefix cache TTL (0s) which removed cache warm entries and reduced batch window -> cache miss storm + smaller batches -> throughput collapse. Autoscaler couldn't compensate because pool_max_nodes was hit.

Anna (oncall): current status at 09:52 UTC: queue depth back to baseline (~150), prefix cache hit ~75%, latency near normal, no ongoing throttles. Keeping incident open for observation and handoff.

Ravi: running follow-ups:
- increase e2e monitor sensitivity for prefix_cache_ttl regressions
- add pre-deploy validation to detect zero TTL changes in batch/cache configs
- temporary playbook update: autoscaler overrides allowed by oncall with two-person approval

Marta: I've scheduled a canary gating job for config rollouts so future max_batch_window and prefix_cache_ttl changes must pass perf test before majority rollout.

Anna (oncall): handing to Ravi for 4h watch and verification of regression tests. Ravi will own postmortem and customer impact summary.

Ravi: taking handoff at 10:02 UTC. I'll consolidate timeline, attach logs, and produce postmortem with root cause, remediation, and follow-up owner assignments.

Deploy-bot: auto-notify: postmortem owner assigned=Ravi, target-ETA=2026-03-16 18:00 UTC

Anna (oncall): good job team. Closing pager but leaving thread live for postmortem comments.

Pagerbot: RESOLVED: incident_eu_west_gpu_high #1767890123 status=resolved resolved_at=1767891350

Sam R: notes to add to postmortem: include `git diff` of the rollout change, exact metric graphs (prefix hit-rate, batch size, queue depth), and timeline of autoscaler errors. Also recommend creating an automated preflight check to reject `prefix_cache_ttl <= 0` or require explicit rationale.

Ravi: acknowledged. I'll include impact table for customers (anonymized), SLA hit estimates, and recommended compensation for affected enterprise customers.

Marta: will follow up on status page updates and support comms.

Anna (oncall): handoff complete. If anything regresses, ping me directly.

-- end of thread --
